newsitem.title: UK: Blenheim to mesh well with United.
newsitem.headline: Blenheim to mesh well with United.

text.p: United News' agreed offer for international exhibitions group Blenheim is a good strategic move and the price paid is reasonable given the recent bid speculation surrounding the stock, analysts said on Tuesday.
"After VNU's move, United have done well to tie it up at five pounds a share," said David Forster of Salomon Brothers.
"In Miller Freeman, United have a substantial established business in this area and Blenheim will fit well into it."
United offered five pounds per ordinary share in a deal which valued Blenheim at 592.5 million stg. United said it had acceptances for 51 percent of its target.
United News and Anglo-Dutch group Reed-Elsevier had been seen as the two principal suitors for in a takeover saga that has dragged on for four months.
But Dutch publishing group VNU stirred the pot last week when it paid five pounds per share to acquire a 15 percent stake in Blenheim in a dawn raid.
VNU said on Tuesday that it would not make a counter bid and sources close to Reed Elsevier have acknowledged in the last few days that the company was out of the running.
Blenheim's powerful presence in continental Europe, France in particular, makes it a good complement to Miller Freeman.
France was Blenheim's largest source of revenue in 1995, providing 37 percent of its income, followed by the U.S. with 26 percent and the UK with 20 percent.

Miller Freeman is active in Europe, the U.S. and Asia but the American market is seen as its main strength. Miller Freeman operates over 100 exhibitions, supported by a range of business and trade publications while Blenheim has over 170 exhibitions but lacks a significant publishing portfolio.
The combination of the two units will create the world's largest trade exhibition group with 1995 pro forma turnover of 545.5 million stg and operating profit of 88 million.
United said the deal should be earnings enhancing from next year.
United said "significant" cost savings could be achieved and analysts said these could be worth some 10 million stg when surplus property was taken into account.

Lorna Tilbian of Panmure Gordon said that the deal should generate some real revenue growth. "The real excitement is when you look at the combined revenue to be produced from access to new geographical areas and and new market segments."
Blenheim said two weeks ago that current trading was ahead of budget and that its strong performance would last into 1997.
It this month reported interim pre-tax profit on ordinary activities of 30.7 million stg on turnover of 102.8 million.
The deal is United's first big acquisition since it merged with MAI this year to create a media major with interests ranging from national newspapers to commercial television.
United News operates the commercial television (ITV) franchises for southern and eastern England and some analysts believe it eyeing HTV HTV.L, the ITV company for south-west England and Wales.
New legislation makes it possible for United to acquire more than its current two ITV licences.
Panmure Gordon's Tilbian said debt levels after the Blenheim deal left United room to go for HTV if it wanted.
HTV, long rumoured as a bid target for a number of UK companies, has a market capitalisation of some 325 million stg.
United said the deal left it with pro forma net debt at June 30 of 625 million stg and interest cover of 7.2 times.
-- Keith Weir, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
